question: What is called covering, and what exists even before the Śiva-named principle?
premises: Covering is called that which ends in power, as long as it exists.
Although before, even in the principle named Śiva, there is the world-path.
inference: Covering is power-limited and persists while existent; the world-path is present even prior to the Śiva-named principle.
uncertainties: "śaktyantaṃ" may mean "ending in power" or "limited by power".
The exact syntactic force of "prāk" and the scope of "bhuvanapaddhatiḥ" are not fully clear.
plain_english: They call 'covering' that which ends in power, as long as it exists; although before, even in the principle called Śiva, there is the world-path.
